# Isolde Pembroke

## Overview

- **Age:** Eighteen years old
- **Gender:** Female

## Appearance

Isolde is a young woman with dark hair, dark eyes, and a neat, rosy appearance. She has a refined taste in attire and often dresses in attractive gowns.

_Sources: [v1 c25 P4](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0004)_

## Personality

Pragmatic, sweet, cheerful, and creative, Isolde enjoys city life and harbors a loyal, deeply affectionate nature toward her close friends. Though she is a diligent worker and helper, she occasionally worries about culinary mistakes, social standing, and speaking with improper grammar.

_Sources: [v2 c26 P45](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0045)_

## Traits

- Pragmatic and sweet
- Cheerful and creative
- Prefers city life
- Fear of living as an old maid  <sub>[v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056)</sub>

## Abilities

- Singing solos in choir  <sub>[v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)</sub>
- Crocheting and teaching crochet
- Dressmaking and home decoration
- Crafting red tissue paper bookmarks

## Goals

- To remain devoted companions with Nell Harcourt  <sub>[v2 c26 P45](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0045)</sub>

## History

Isolde grew up residing in rural locations such as Larkrise, Grey Shutters, and Pear Hill. At Brierley School, she became the devoted desk mate, classmate, and bosom friend of Nell Harcourt, sharing schoolwork, singing lessons, and personal secrets. During her childhood, she participated in school concerts, served on local committees like the B.V.I.S., and wrote for a story club. Their friendship experienced a temporary strain when Isolde accidentally drank currant wine, leading her mother to restrict their meetings, though their emotional bond endured. Isolde later attended school at Wexcombe and eventually became engaged to Gideon.

_Sources: [v1 c17 P39](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0039), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Pembroke and niece of Miss Lavinia Pembroke
- Named at birth by a former schoolmaster who lodged at her father's home
- Attended Brierley School and Wexcombe

## Quotes

> However, Wexcombe will have a great number of smart girls, whereas I am merely an unintelligent little girl from the country who occasionally says ‘I seen’. . . even if I actually am aware of the correct phrasing whenever I pause to consider it.  <sub>[v2 c26 P45](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0045)</sub>

> Oh, I guess dying would not be very difficult; living as an old maid is what I would dismally dislike,  <sub>[v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056)</sub>


## Affiliations

- Brierley School — Student
- Brierley Village Improvement Society (B.V.I.S.) — Committee member
